Card Name: RULE 1 — Deliverable = internal line-item AUDIT MEMO for Joseph (Gmail draft, not a letter to the OA)
Card Description:
OA Position Review output = a line-item AUDIT MEMO for Joseph's internal use, NOT a letter/checklist addressed to the OA. Save as a Gmail DRAFT (never send). To: blank unless Joseph named a recipient. Subject: "OA Position Review — [Insured Last] — [Carrier] [Claim #]". Sections, always in this order, never merged/reordered:
• HEADER — one line, all three totals + gap: "OA $RCV/$ACV · Carrier (adjuster) $RCV/$ACV · Ours (estimator) $RCV"; then "Gap between our estimate and the OA: $X".
• S1 — carrier line items missing from the OA (qty + $ each). If the OA carried everything forward, say "None" plainly and explain it means nothing carrier-conceded is in dispute (fight is only over what exceeds carrier scope). Then bullet what the OA ADDED beyond the carrier — his admissions/leverage (include qty, grade, and R&R upgrades).
• S2 — OUR items the OA didn't include, in four labeled groups: (a) Pure omissions — qty + our RCV incl O&P each; group by trade if long; subtotal. (b) Scope disputes — both sides' numbers + delta, largest first. (c) Material/grade downgrades — 2-col table (ours vs his). (d) Quantity gaps on shared items — 2-col table; include gaps in HIS favor too and say so.
• S3 — structural (RULES 3 & 5).
• S4 — Reconciliation (MANDATORY): pure omissions + scope deltas + O&P vs the header RCV gap; if they don't roughly reconcile, say so and name what's unaccounted.
Style: dollar figures to the cent exactly as printed; our RCV includes O&P (say so once); short bold item names then numbers; tables for grade/qty; no narrative paragraphs, no closing summary, no hedging. Card Name: RULE 2 — Matching rules: get the match right before calling anything missing
Card Description:
Before listing anything as missing/omitted, resolve the match — this is the whole job:
• R&R vs split pairs: "R&R X" = "Remove X" + "X". Not an omission.
• Combined vs split lines: compare TOTALS, not line counts (our 242LF gutter + 112LF downspout = his 350LF "gutter/downspout").
• Different names, same work: "Tear off/haul comp shingles" ≈ "Remove Laminated comp shingle w/felt"; "R&R Furnace vent — rain cap + storm collar" partially covers "R&R Rain cap". Call these PARTIAL coverage, note what the narrower line leaves out — not an omission.
• Buried scope: eave starter inside a shingle line's waste calc is NOT a paid starter course; removal "included in the shingle removal" per a carrier note is still a scope position worth flagging. Read the option strings + italic notes UNDER the line items — that's where these hide.
• Coverage buckets: Contents, Other Structures, Dwelling are separate — an entire coverage at $0.00 in his estimate is an omission, not an oversight to gloss over.
• NEVER invent a line item — everything traces to a document in front of you; no assumed damage, no "he probably should have included it."
• Always list "items he has that we don't" in S3 — credits to offset our adds; we lose credibility if the panel finds them first. (Taught by Joseph 8/3/26 — uploaded OA Position Review instructions.)

Card Name: 📝 NOTE — Google Drive search_files query syntax (tool quirk)
Card Description:
Operational discovery (Krowski/Benoit run, 2026-08-08):

The Google_Drive search_files tool REJECTS several query forms with "Unsupported query field": bare keywords (e.g. `Krowski`), `name contains '...'`, a separate `parentId` argument, and `'FOLDER_ID' in parents`.

What WORKS (Drive API q-style): `fullText contains 'X'`; `mimeType = 'application/pdf'`; `mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder'`; combine with `and`. Folder NAMES are matched by `fullText contains` (found the "Randy Benoit" folder that way). To read a specific file's full text use read_file_content with fileId.

Caveat: image-only/scanned PDFs have no fullText, so keyword search won't surface them — fall back to list_recent_files or the shared root folder, then OCR (see the scanned-OA-PDF note).

(Discovered by AI agent, 2026-08-08 run.)

Card Name: 📝 NOTE — OCR scanned PDFs without context bloat (download_file_content saves base64 to a file)
Card Description:
Operational discovery (Whitney run, 2026-08-22):

When a scanned/image-only PDF is too big for read_file_content, download_file_content now REFUSES to inline the base64 and instead SAVES it to a local file path (it tells you the path). Don't try to read that path into context — process it in bash:
1) python3: json.load the saved file, base64.b64decode data['content'] → write .pdf
2) pdftoppm -r 200 -png file.pdf out/pg
3) tesseract each png stdout --psm 6 > ocr.txt
This kept a 4.6MB / 15-page scanned demand (Whitney "ANGELA WHITNEY.pdf", TX INSURANCE APPRAISER, image-only) entirely out of the model context and produced clean line-item + summary text (RCV/O&P/deprec all readable). tesseract 5.3.4 + pdftoppm/pdfinfo are preinstalled in the run environment.
